Rashi on Shabbat 146b:10:1.english: And he did not have room - in the house for the seating place of [the] students.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:10:2.hebrew: ומשום כבוד רבותינו - שלא היה להן דבר לישב עליו, ויושבין על גבי קרקע:
Rashi on Shabbat 146b:10:2.english: And out of respect for our Rabbis - For they did not have anything to sit upon, and were sitting on the ground.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:10:3.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi - They were his student-colleagues.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:11:1.english: Into the pit - That has no water in it.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:11:2.english: That it will be protected - So that it will not spoil because of the heat.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:11:3.hebrew: ואת המים היפים ברעים - כלי מלא מים יפים לתוך מקוה מים רעים, להשתמר שיצונו ולא יחמו:
Rashi on Shabbat 146b:11:3.english: And the good water into the bad [water] - [One places] a vessel full of good water into a pool of bad water, to be preserved so that it cools off and does not become warm.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:11:4.english: Someone whose [garments] fell - That they fell into water on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:11:5.hebrew: לחצר החיצונה - הסמוכה למבוא העיר, בתוך העיר, שהוא מקום משתמר:
Rashi on Shabbat 146b:11:5.english: To the outer courtyard - [The courtyard] adjacent to the entrance of the city, within the city, which is a guarded place.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:11:6.english: He spreads them in the sun - To dry them.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:11:7.english: But not opposite the masses - For they will suspect him of having laundered them.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:12:1.english: [It is] obvious - that one may place cooked food into the pit.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:12:2.english: Holes - That are in the floor of the pit, so that they will be level to set down the pot.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:1:1.hebrew: משום ריחשא - שלא יכנס בו שרץ, כגון נמייה וחולדה, שממיתים את התרנגולים:
Rashi on Shabbat 146b:1:1.english: Because of vermin - So that a creeping creature will not enter it [the coop], such as a marten and a rat, which kill the chickens.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:1:2.english: Sometimes one did not prepare it initially - so that it would be [large] enough to let out the vapor and let in the air.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:2:1.english: They only taught - that one may perforate.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:2:2.hebrew: אלא במקום - דסתימה זו לא נעשית אלא לשמור ריח היין שלא יצא ויתקלקל, וכיון דלאו סתימה מעליותא עבדי לה, לאו כלום הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 146b:2:2.english: Only in a place - For this sealing is only made to preserve the aroma of the wine so that it does not escape and spoil; and since they do not make a proper sealing for it, it is nothing.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:2:3.hebrew: לחזק - שיחזק הכלי שלא יצא יינו. הואיל וסתימה מעלייתא היא, כי הדר נקיב לה, הוי כפותח לכתחלה:
Rashi on Shabbat 146b:2:3.english: To reinforce - [Meaning] that he reinforces the vessel so that its wine will not come out. Since it is a proper seal, when he pierces it again, it is like opening [a hole] for the first time.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:2:4.hebrew: למטה מן היין נמי לשמר הוא - כיון דלאו כובד היין נשען עליו, סגי ליה בסתימה כל דהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 146b:2:4.english: [A hole] below the wine is also [considered] to preserve - Since the weight of the wine does not rest upon it, a minimal seal suffices for it.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:2:5.hebrew: למטה מן השמרים - אצל שוליו, שכל כובד היין נשען שם:
Rashi on Shabbat 146b:2:5.english: Below the sediment - Near its bottom, where all the weight of the wine rests.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:3:1.english: [A baraita] was taught that supports you - That the designation of an entrance does not depart from it except through a proper sealing.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:3:2.hebrew: בית סתום יש לו ד"א - קיי"ל בבבא בתרא: חצר מתחלקת לפי פתחיה, לפי פתח הבתים הפתוחין לה. אם באו לחלק את החצר בין שנים, שהיה לזה בית שפתוחין לו לחצר שני פתחים ולזה בית שפתוחין לו לחצר ד' פתחים, נוטל לכל פתח ארבע אמות בחצר נגד פתחו, למדת רוחב פתחו, והשאר חולקין בשוה. ואם נסתם אחד מהם קודם חלוקת החצר, ולא פירץ את פצימיו אלא סתם בין שני הפצימין, אינו מפסיד [דין] פתחו בכך. פירץ את פצימיו ואח"כ סתמו, פקע שם פתח מיניה:
Rashi on Shabbat 146b:3:2.english: A sealed house has four cubits - We hold in Bava Batra [that] a courtyard is divided according to its entrances, [that is,] according to the entrance[s] of the houses that open into it. If they come to divide the courtyard between two [owners] — where this one had a house with two entrances opening into the courtyard and that one had a house with four entrances opening into the courtyard — [each] takes four cubits in the courtyard opposite his entrance for each entrance, to the measure of the width of his entrance, and the rest they divide equally. And if one of them was sealed before the division of the courtyard, and he did not break its doorposts, but rather sealed between the two doorposts, he does not lose [the legal status of] his entrance thereby. [If] he broke its doorposts and afterward sealed it, the designation of an entrance has departed from it.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:3:3.english: A sealed house - and [when] a corpse is inside it, it does not render its surroundings ritually impure.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:3:4.hebrew: פרץ פצימיו - וסתמו, נעשה קבר ומטמא סביביו ד"א, כדאמר בסוטה (ד' מד.): מת תופס ד"א לטומאה. וגזרה דרבנן, שמא יאהיל ולא יבין:
Rashi on Shabbat 146b:3:4.english: One broke its doorposts - and sealed it: it becomes a grave and renders its surroundings ritually impure [for] four cubits, as it is said in Sotah (44a): a corpse occupies four cubits with respect to ritual impurity. And [this is] a rabbinic decree, lest one overshadow [it] and not realize [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:4:1.english: A tube - To insert a hollow reed into the hole of the barrel so that the wine will come out through the reed.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:4:2.english: Cutting - Trimming [Old French: rognier] to fit it to the size of the hole.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:4:4.english: And not fitted - It has not [yet] been placed into the hole to know whether it is [of] its [proper] size.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:6:1.english: If you say [it refers] to the first clause - [that is,] to cut it and smooth it.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:8:1.hebrew: טרפא דאסא - לתת עלה של הדס בנקב החבית, שהעלה עשוי כמרזב והיין זב דרך שם:
Rashi on Shabbat 146b:8:1.english: A myrtle leaf - [It is prohibited] to place a myrtle leaf in the hole of the barrel, for the leaf is shaped like a spout and the wine flows through there.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:8:2.english: A decree due to a spout - Lest he prepare a spout.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:8:3.hebrew: שמא יקטום - העלה מן הענף. וכיון דקטמיה, הוה ליה כמתקן כלי, כדתניא במסכת ביצה (דף לג:): לחצות בו שיניו לא יקטמנו, ואם קטמו חייב חטאת:
Rashi on Shabbat 146b:8:3.english: Lest one cut - the leaf from the branch. And once he cuts it, it is like fashioning a utensil, as it is taught [in a baraita] in Tractate Beitzah (33b): [With regard to a piece of wood] to pick one's teeth with it, he may not cut it, and if he cut it, he is liable [to bring] a sin-offering.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:9:1.hebrew: בי סדיא - לבדין שקורין פלטר"ש, ועשויין לקפלן תחתיו במקום הכר או הכסת:
Rashi on Shabbat 146b:9:1.english: Bei sadya - Felts, which are called "feltres" [in Old French], and are made to be folded beneath oneself in place of a pillow or a cushion.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:9:2.english: Rav prohibited - to bring it as a garment through a public domain while wrapped in it.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:9:3.english: With soft [ones] - For it is customary to warm oneself with them.

Rashi on Shabbat 146b:9:4.english: That they are permitted - For they are a garment.

Tosafot on Shabbat 146b:10:1.hebrew: אייתי ליה בי סדיא - בי מיצעי הוה, דאי לאו הכי היכי איתמר מכללא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 146b:10:1.english: "They brought him a pillow" - It was an intermediate [pillow], for if it were not so, how would [Rav's opinion] have been stated by inference?

Tosafot on Shabbat 146b:11:1.hebrew: מי שנשרו כליו במים - "בדרך" גרסינן; לשון נפילה, לא כפי' הקונטרס לעיל בפרק במה אשה (שבת דף סה.) שנשרו במי גשמים, דהא אמרינן בביצה בפרק משילין (ביצה דף לה:): מאן דתני מנשירין לא משתבש, כדתנן מי שנשרו כליו במים בדרך — אלמא לשון נפילה הוא. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 146b:11:1.english: Someone whose garments fell [nashru] into water - We read [the text with the word] "on the road" [baderekh]. [Nashru is] an expression of falling, not like the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi] above in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Ishah (Shabbat 65a), [where he explained] that they were soaked [nishru] in rainwater; for we say in Beitzah in the chapter [entitled] Mashilin (Beitzah 35b): "One who teaches [the version] manashirin is not mistaken, as we learned in the Mishnah: 'Someone whose garments fell [nashru] into water on the road'" — thus, it is an expression of falling. [From the mouth of my teacher.]

Tosafot on Shabbat 146b:1:1.hebrew: משום ריחשא - ואטו פתחא אחרינא דליכא למיחש לריחשא לא גזרינן? דדוקא אטו לול של תרנגולין גזרינן, דלא מסקי אינשי אדעתייהו שיהא עשוי להכניס ולהוציא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 146b:1:1.english: Because of vermin - And on account of another [type of] opening where there is no concern for vermin, do we not issue a decree [against adding]? [No,] for specifically on account of a chicken coop do we decree, since people do not realize that it is made for bringing in and taking out:

Tosafot on Shabbat 146b:3:1.hebrew: פרץ פצימיו מטמא כל סביביו - פי' בקונטרס: כל סביביו — ד' אמות כקבר. ואין נראה לזקיני הרב ר' שמשון זצ"ל, דכיון דמסיימי מחיצתא ולית לן למיחש שמא יעלה על הבית ויאהיל עליו ולא ידע, לית לן למימר דמטמא ד' אמות כל סביביו; כדמוכח בסוטה פרק משוח מלחמה (סוטה ד' מד.) גבי חצר הקבר: "העומד בתוכה טהור"; "הני מילי חצר הקבר דמסיימא מחיצתא, אבל מת בעלמא תפיס", ומשמע דבמת נמי היכא דמסיימא לא נטמא כל סביביו ד' אמות. אלא נראה לו דהכי פי': זיזין באותו בית שבולטין מחוץ לבית מכל צד, ויש בהם פותח טפח בכל אחד. אם הבית סתום ועדיין נראית בו צורת הפתח, אינו מטמא, שסתמו של מת עומד לצאת דרך הפתח; פרץ פצימיו וחזר ובנאו כשאר כותל ולא נותר בו כלל פתח — מטמא כל סביביו, דכל חד וחד איכא לספוקי דילמא דרך אותו מקום יצא מן הבית. מיהו לאו פירכא היא כולי האי מה שהקשה לפירוש הקונטרס, די"ל שלא חלקו חכמים במת. ועוד נראה דלא קשה כלל לפי' הקונטרס, דבית נמי לא מסיימי מחיצתא, שהוא מטמא הנוגע בכתלים אפילו לא יעלה על גביו, כקבר שמטמא במגע אפילו מן הצד; כדתניא בספרי בפרשת פרה אדומה: "או בקבר — זה קבר סתום; או אינו אלא קבר פתוח? אמרת ק"ו: ומה אהל שמקבל טומאה אינו מטמא מכל צדדין כשהוא פתוח, קבר שאינו מקבל טומאה אינו דין שלא יטמא מכל צדדין כשהוא פתוח?!"; אלמא כשהוא סתום מטמא אף הנוגע מן הצד:
Tosafot on Shabbat 146b:3:1.english: [If] one broke its doorposts, it renders all of its surroundings ritually impure - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: [This means] all of its surroundings [for] four cubits, like a grave. But this does not appear [correct] to my grandfather, the Rabbi, R' Shimshon, of blessed memory, because since the partitions [of the house] are clearly marked, and we do not need to be concerned lest someone climb onto the house and overshadow it without knowing, we should not say that it renders impure four cubits all around it; as is proven in Sotah, chapter Meshuach Milchamah (Sotah 44a), regarding the courtyard of a tomb: "One who stands inside it is ritually pure" — [and the Gemara explains:] "This applies only to the courtyard of a tomb, whose partitions are clearly marked, whereas an ordinary corpse takes up [four cubits]" — which implies that with an ordinary corpse as well, wherever [the boundaries] are clearly marked, it does not render impure four cubits all around it. Rather, it appears to him that this is the explanation: [There are] projections on that house that protrude outside the house on every side, each having [an area of] a handbreadth squared. If the house is sealed, yet the form of the doorway is still visible in it, it does not render [the projections] impure, because ordinarily a corpse is destined to be carried out through the doorway. [However, if] one broke its doorposts and rebuilt it like the rest of the wall, so that no doorway remains in it at all, it renders all of its surroundings impure, because for each and every [projection] there is room for doubt that perhaps [the corpse] will exit the house through that spot. However, what he objected to the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi] is not such a [strong] refutation, for one can say that the Sages did not differentiate regarding a corpse. Furthermore, it appears that there is no difficulty at all with the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], for [with] a house too its partitions are not [considered] demarcated, since it renders impure one who touches the walls even if he does not climb on top of it, like a grave that renders impure through contact even from the side; as it is taught in the Sifrei in the portion of Parah Adumah: "'Or a grave' — this refers to a sealed grave. Or is it rather an open grave? You can say [via] a kal vachomer: If a tent, which is susceptible to ritual impurity, does not render impure from all sides when it is open, then a grave, which is not susceptible to ritual impurity, is it not logical that it should not render impure from all sides when it is open?!" Thus, when it is sealed, it renders impure even one who touches it from the side.

Tosafot on Shabbat 146b:6:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yoshiya - Therefore, it is permitted from the outset to place a tube, which is called razel, into a barrel.

Tosafot on Shabbat 146b:8:1.hebrew: משום מרזב - פי' הרב פור"ת: שלא יבוא ליתן על גגו מרזב. וקשה, דבגובתא נמי נגזר. אלא נראה לרבי כפי' הקונט': שלא יתקן מרזב ליינו, שיפול היין בתוכו וילך למרחוק, דכשלוקח עלה של הדס ומקפלו כעין מרזב, נראה כעושה מרזב; אבל בגובתא, שאינו עושה בו שום מעשה, לא גזרינן. מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 146b:8:1.english: Due to a spout [marzev] - Rabbi Porat explained: [It is a decree] lest one come to place a gutter on his roof. And [this] is difficult, for in [the case of] a reed tube as well we should issue a decree. Rather, it appears to the Rabbi like the explanation of Rashi: [it is a decree] lest one fashion a spout for his wine, so that the wine falls into it and flows to a distance; for when one takes a myrtle leaf and folds it like a spout, it appears as though he is making a spout, but with a reed tube, where he does not perform any act [of shaping] on it, we do not issue a decree. [From my teacher.]
